sections.html:
An Orangetown homeowner has three realistic paths: hire an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer. Speed depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you must close. Villages sit inside the town, so work out which government actually covers your street before anything else.

Orangetown occupies the southeastern edge of Rockland County, bordered by the Hudson on one side and New Jersey on another. Its population was 50,377 on July 1, 2025. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $638,100 and make up 74.2% of housing. Median gross rent is $2,015 a month and median household income is $145,007. With prices like these, a repair bill or a slipped closing date costs real money, so set a firm cash figure beside whatever a listing would leave you after repairs, commissions and months of carrying costs.

Buyers who commute will ask about transit. Pearl River station has New Jersey Transit service on the Pascack Valley Line, and I-87 runs through town as the New York State Thruway. Look at the school district named on your tax bill, because many buyers filter by it.

sections.h2: Which parts of Orangetown does the town government cover?
sections.html:
Town government in Orangetown serves the unincorporated hamlets. Nyack, Piermont and Grand View-on-Hudson are villages that run their own local affairs. Building safety in the unincorporated areas falls to the town's Building Department.

The hamlets are Blauvelt, Nauraushaun, Orangeburg, Pearl River, Palisades, South Nyack, Sparkill, Tappan and Upper Grandview. South Nyack was a village from 1878 until 2022. A house inside one of the villages has its permit history at that village hall, so begin your records request there.

Plenty of everyday projects in Orangetown call for both a permit and a certificate of occupancy, even ones owners think of as upkeep. The department's list covers:

  • Additions, interior alterations and decks
  • Hot tubs, pools, fireplaces and chimneys
  • Oil and gas heating units and tanks
  • Retaining walls and solar panels
  • Central air conditioners and ductless units
  • Window and door replacement
  • Sheds over 100 square feet in residential districts

An application needs fees, a survey or plot plan, and contractor details: a Rockland County license plus workers' compensation and disability coverage. Building without a permit can bring prosecution and fines, so settle any past project that never got a final sign-off before you put the house on the market. Zoning-based denials go to the independent Zoning Board of Appeals. Call the department at (845) 359-8410.

Chapter 15 of the town code adds a certificate of compliance for property uses other than one- and two-family homes, and that certificate cannot be transferred to a new owner. Selling a single-family house falls outside it. Owners of multi-unit or commercial buildings should ask the department what applies to them before signing a contract.

sections.h2: Tax bills, due dates and penalties
sections.html:
Two bills arrive each year: town and county in January, school in the fall. One combined office now handles both the Town Clerk's work and tax collection.

Orangetown tax collection windows
BillMailing and due dateLate penalty
Town and countyMailed in early January for January 1 to December 31. Pay through January 31.1% through February 28, then 2% through March 31
SchoolMailed in early September for July 1 to June 30. Due September 30.5% until collection ends, usually October 31

After March 31, town and county bills left unpaid are passed to the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance. School bills end up there as well, and once the re-levy date arrives they reappear on the following year's property tax bill carrying a 7% penalty plus interest. The Orangetown tax office takes school tax payments for the Pearl River, South Orangetown, Nyack and Nanuet districts.

Village and school charges that went unpaid can be re-levied onto the property tax bill. Another trap: an exemption the previous owner had, which the new owner was not entitled to, can come back as a prorated charge. Either one can show up late in the sale.

Request a written balance from the tax office well ahead of closing and hand a copy to whoever is handling the paperwork. Whatever remains unpaid is normally settled from your sale proceeds on closing day, and knowing the number early keeps it from holding up the deed.

The population climbed from 26,662 in 1940 to 53,533 in 1970, dipped to 46,742 by 1990, and was 48,655 in 2020. A lot of local housing dates to that mid-century boom. Your tax record lists the year built, and an older date points a buyer's inspector toward the heating, wiring and plumbing.

Terrain is uneven: rocky hills to the east, and the Nyack Hills climbing 300 to 500 feet beside the river. A retaining wall needs a permit, so if yours stands on a slope, check that it has one before listing.

The Rockland County Clerk records the deed when an Orangetown house sells, and the seller owes New York transfer tax at $2 for each $500 of price. Land records at the clerk's office are searchable online at any hour, a handy way to see exactly what is on file against your property.

File Form TP-584 with the clerk of the county where the house stands. Both the form and the tax must be in within 15 days after the deed is delivered. Homes selling for $1 million or more carry an extra one percent tax, which the buyer pays. Your attorney or title company normally drafts the deed and fills out the return.

Inherited the place? A transfer by devise, bequest or inheritance does not count as a taxable conveyance under state rules. Your attorney can tell you how the estate paperwork lines up with the sale date.

A fast closing mostly depends on documents being ready. Collect these first:

  • The current town and county bill and school bill, with a written balance from the tax office
  • Permits and certificates of occupancy for earlier projects such as decks, pools, heating units and retaining walls
  • Your deed, and any survey or plot plan you have
  • A New York attorney or title company ready to prepare the deed and the TP-584

With a cash buyer there is no lender appraisal or loan approval to wait for, which leaves title work, the deed and recording at the Rockland County Clerk. Insist on a written offer, agree on who pays each closing charge, and let your attorney review the contract first. Transfer tax and any tax payoff remain the seller's job.

faqs.q: Does the Orangetown Building Department cover every address in the town?
faqs.a: No. The town's building authority covers the unincorporated hamlets. Nyack, Piermont and Grand View-on-Hudson are incorporated villages that run their own local government.

faqs.q: When are Orangetown school taxes due?
faqs.a: September 30. After that a 5% penalty runs until collection closes, usually October 31, and bills still open go to the Rockland County Commissioner of Finance.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace windows in Orangetown?
faqs.a: Yes, windows and doors are on the town's permit list, along with a certificate of occupancy. A quick call to the Building Department settles any doubt.

faqs.q: Where is the deed recorded after an Orangetown sale?
faqs.a: At the Rockland County Clerk's office. Transfer tax of $2 per $500 falls on the seller, and Form TP-584 must be filed within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a building permit denial in Orangetown?
faqs.a: Take it to the Zoning Board of Appeals, which is independent of the department. It hears permits turned down for zoning noncompliance and weighs each case on its own facts.
